approval_timeline.complex: 2-4 weeks for commercial plan review in Charlotte/Mecklenburg County, longer if revisions are needed.
approval_timeline.simple: Commercial TI/addition/remodel scopes usually require plan review; expect at least several business days to a few weeks depending on completeness, valuation, and local queue.

checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in NC
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Equipment spec sheets / submittal documents for all new units
Load calculation (Manual J) if replacing system >5 tons or changing capacity
Refrigerant type and charge amount documentation
Energy compliance form (required in many states — check NC requirements)

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed North Carolina contractor pulls the permit on the owner/tenant's behalf, and the contractor license number must appear on the application. For HVAC, an NC H1-H5 licensed HVAC contractor pulls the mechanical permit. For plumbing, an NC licensed plumbing contractor pulls the plumbing permit. For the building permit, the appropriate NC-licensed general contractor or authorized commercial builder pulls the permit if the scope requires it.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to Mecklenburg County Code Enforcement

common_mistakes: Submitting the commercial TI without plan review documents — first-generation retail upfits with restroom and HVAC are not simple OTC trade permits
Forgetting the plumbing permit for the new restroom because the shell space is already plumbed nearby
Starting demolition or framing before the permit is issued and posted at the site

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city/county registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

response_body.inspection_booking: Schedule inspections through the Mecklenburg County Code Enforcement permitting/inspections portal at or by calling (704) 336-3300. Commercial work is typically scheduled with advance notice; plan on at least 24 hours minimum and confirm the current cutoff time with the inspector assigned to the permit. Use the permit number and inspection type when booking.

inspections.description: Inspector verifies duct layout, equipment location, outside air/return air provisions, condensate drainage, equipment clearances, fire/smoke damper locations if applicable, and that the system matches approved plans.

pro_tips: Pull the building permit first, then attach the mechanical and plumbing scopes to the same project record so plan review stays coordinated.
Have the HVAC equipment schedule and restroom fixture count finalized before submittal — Mecklenburg plan reviewers will kick back incomplete commercial TI packages.
Check your Charlotte/Mecklenburg contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
For a $410,000 commercial upfit, expect plan review comments on accessibility, egress, and restroom compliance; clean drawings save weeks.

response_body.zoning_hoa_flag: Commercial retail tenant upfits can be delayed by zoning, occupancy, parking, accessibility, and any change-of-use review. If the shell building is in a historic district or overlay, exterior signage, storefront changes, or façade work may need separate approval. HOA restrictions are usually not the issue for commercial retail, but lease and landlord approval often are.
